macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street ends mixed as Fed signals further tightening
items.summary: The Dow fell 1.12% to 50,193.03 and the S&P 500 declined 0.24% to 7,322.53, while the Nasdaq gained 0.39% to 24,429.89. Investors reacted to hawkish Federal Reserve minutes indicating that nearly all officials expected further rate increases, with some open to a larger hike if inflation remains elevated.

items.title: Fed Governor Waller raises possibility of 50-basis-point December hike
items.summary: Christopher Waller said the Federal Reserve may need more aggressive action against inflation, including a potential 50-basis-point increase at the December meeting or stronger guidance for additional hikes in 2027. Markets were pricing roughly a 90% probability of a 25-basis-point December increase.

items.title: Anthropic prices record-breaking IPO at $83 per share
items.summary: AI company Anthropic priced its initial public offering above the marketed range at $83 per share, raising approximately $81 billion and setting a reported record for the largest stock-market debut. The offering helped lift U.S. equity futures despite broader concerns about AI valuations.

items.title: Nvidia beats estimates but shares fall
items.summary: Nvidia reported quarterly results above analyst expectations and issued a revenue outlook exceeding forecasts, but its shares fell about 2.9% as investors remained concerned about AI-stock valuations and leadership uncertainty following reports involving co-founder Jensen Huang.

items.title: Asian markets slide amid AI and rate concerns
items.summary: MSCI’s broadest Asia-Pacific index excluding Japan fell 1.7% toward a seven-month low, while Taiwan’s benchmark dropped 4.6% and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng declined nearly 2%. Investors weighed the prospect of prolonged U.S. monetary tightening against concerns about elevated AI investment and valuations.

items.title: European shares edge higher as Anthropic IPO offsets Fed concerns
items.summary: The STOXX Europe 600 rose about 0.3% in fragile trading. The record Anthropic offering provided some support, while investors also assessed unexpectedly firmer euro-area core inflation of 2.6% and the prospect of tighter U.S. monetary policy.

items.title: Oil prices fall to lowest level since August
items.summary: U.S. crude oil prices dropped 3.2% to $83.26 a barrel, their lowest settlement since August 26, adding to the day’s broader market volatility.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Crypto market falls as Bitcoin nears $60,000
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 2.15% to roughly $61,635, while Ethereum declined 1.64% to $1,746 and Solana dropped 1.56% to $72.47. The sell-off was linked to hawkish Federal Reserve minutes, broader market weakness and declining ETF demand.

items.title: Crypto prices remain volatile amid ETF outflows
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $63,700 after recovering from a low near $62,000, while U.S.-listed Bitcoin products recorded approximately $306 million in outflows. Ethereum reclaimed the $1,800 level despite continued weekly losses.

items.title: Hong Kong regulator adds Hyperliquid to alert list
items.summary: Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission warned that decentralized derivatives exchange Hyperliquid lacks a local license and may be marketing services to Hong Kong residents.

items.title: Russian rules open access to major crypto assets for retail investors
items.summary: New rules reportedly allow Russian retail investors to buy Bitcoin, Ether and Tether’s USDt through approved trading institutions, although technical, custody and investor-testing obstacles remain.

items.title: Variational raises $110 million for onchain derivatives platform
items.summary: Onchain derivatives protocol Variational completed a $110 million funding round at a reported $1.5 billion post-money valuation. Bain Capital Crypto led the round, joined by Dragonfly Capital, HSG and Peak XV.

items.title: Bundesbank and Singapore central bank test Cosmos-based settlement
items.summary: Deutsche Bundesbank and the Monetary Authority of Singapore reportedly tested cross-border settlement using Cosmos’s Inter-Blockchain Communication protocol.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon
items.summary: Google reportedly released Gemini 4 Neon, a reasoning model for coding agents, knowledge work, and scientific workflows. It features a 1-million-token context window and is rolling out across the Gemini API, business products, the Gemini app, and Cursor.[2]

items.title: Microsoft launches seven MAI models and Maia 200 accelerator
items.summary: Microsoft introduced seven AI models, including MAI Code 2 for software development, MAI Cyber 2 Flash for cybersecurity, and Decision 1.1 for task routing. The company also said its Maia 200 AI accelerator entered production, emphasizing inference efficiency.[7]

items.title: Anthropic reportedly raises $81 billion in IPO
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly became the first publicly traded frontier AI company after raising $81 billion, with a valuation reported at approximately $1.5 trillion. The debut is being viewed as a major test of investor confidence in enterprise AI and safety-focused model development.[9]

items.title: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max
items.summary: Alibaba launched Qwen4-Max and announced smaller open-weight Qwen4 models, although Qwen4-Max weights may not be publicly released. Chinese AI companies are also increasing filtering of offensive cybersecurity training data.[6]

items.title: AWS makes OpenSearch Memory generally available
items.summary: AWS made Amazon OpenSearch Memory generally available as a serverless persistence layer for AI agents. The service stores interactions, consolidates memories, and retrieves context across sessions using keyword, semantic, and hybrid search.[1]

items.title: AI accelerates AI research and chip design
items.summary: A report citing METR research says frontier-model capabilities are advancing at nearly twice their historical pace, with AI increasingly assisting model developers and researchers. OpenAI and Google also reported AI-assisted gains in chip design and layout workflows.[5]

items.title: Hugging Face open-sources multilingual speech model
items.summary: Hugging Face reportedly open-sourced Rumble-2-Flash under the Apache 2.0 license. The 0.5-billion-parameter speech-recognition model supports more than 40 languages.[1]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches after 13-year wait
items.summary: Rockstar Games began the global rollout of Grand Theft Auto VI, returning players to the Florida-inspired setting of Vice City. The launch is one of the most anticipated entertainment releases in years, with early reviews praising its scale, graphics, detail and player choices.[3][6]

items.title: GTA VI receives near-perfect reviews and strong early sales
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI reportedly earned a 99 Metacritic score and sold more than 17 million copies worldwide shortly after launch, according to early industry estimates. PlayStation accounted for roughly three-quarters of sales, while Take-Two and Sony shares rose amid expectations of a major commercial boost.[6]

items.title: GTA VI launch drives major market and infrastructure attention
items.summary: The release prompted heightened preparation from internet providers because of the game's reported 212-gigabyte download size. Take-Two Interactive shares rose more than 8% as the rollout expanded across international markets.[2]
